scenes.text: You’ve probably seen Swiss cheese in cartoons, completely covered in giant, perfect holes.
It turns out, the secret ingredient was actually tiny specks of hay dust falling into the milk buckets during traditional milking.
Without these microscopic specks to trap the gas, the bubbles can’t form, leaving us with boring, solid cheese.
Would you eat cheese made with deliberate dust? Hit follow for more mind-blowing food secrets!
